MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about 486 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is neither even nor odd
   B. It is odd because it ends in 6
   C. It is even because it ends in 6
   D. It is odd because it has an even number of digits

2. Which is the largest number: 742, 724, 472, 427? (1 mark)
   A. 742
   B. 472
   C. 427
   D. 724

3. In the number 3,850, the digit 8 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Hundreds
   C. Tens
   D. Thousands

4. Which of these shows 190 in words? (1 mark)
   A. nineteen
   B. one hundred and ninety
   C. two hundred and ninety
   D. one hundred and nine

5. Work out 6,003 − 2,475. (1 mark)
   A. 3,428
   B. 3,538
   C. 4,472
   D. 3,528

6. What is the next number in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 4,750
   B. 3,750
   C. 4,000
   D. 4,250

7. Chebet writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 2 5/8
   B. 9/9
   C. 8/3
   D. 5/12

8. Change 7/3 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 2 2/3
   B. 1 2/3
   C. 3 1/3
   D. 2 1/3

9. Chebet writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 5/12
   B. 2 5/8
   C. 9/9
   D. 7/10

10. A rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts and 1 of the parts is shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 1/6
   B. 5/6
   C. 1/5
   D. 6/1

11. Which is greater, 0.3 or 0.29? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. 0.29
   C. It cannot be told
   D. 0.3

12. Ksh 12.50 means (1 mark)
   A. 12 shillings and 5 cents
   B. 1 shilling and 250 cents
   C. 125 shillings
   D. 12 shillings and 50 cents

13. Write 0.75 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 7/5
   B. 75/100
   C. 75/1000
   D. 75/10

14. What is the total value of the digit 7 in 9.27? (1 mark)
   A. 0.007
   B. 0.07
   C. 0.7
   D. 7

15. If k = 3, what is the value of 5k − 2? (1 mark)
   A. 17
   B. 52
   C. 1
   D. 13

16. A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 18 cm
   B. 12 cm
   C. 36 cm
   D. 24 cm

17. Change 5 m 8 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 508 cm
   B. 5,080 cm
   C. 58 cm
   D. 13 cm

18. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 20 m
   B. 18 m
   C. 24 m
   D. 19 m

19. A pencil starts at the 1 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 8 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 6 cm
   B. 9 cm
   C. 8 cm
   D. 7 cm

20. Which shape is a cuboid? (1 mark)
   A. A football
   B. A coin
   C. A plate
   D. A matchbox

21. How many small cubes make a big cube that is 2 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 2 blocks high? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 4
   C. 8
   D. 16

22. What is 4 kg − 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 4 1/4 kg
   D. 4 kg

23. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 11 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 1. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 11:01
   B. 11:55
   C. 11:05
   D. 12:05

24. Change 90 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 1 h
   B. 1 h 30 min
   C. 2 h 30 min
   D. 2 h

25. How long is a lesson that starts at 9:30 a.m. and ends at 12:10 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 50 min
   B. 2 h 40 min
   C. 2 h 25 min
   D. 3 h 40 min

26. How many minutes are in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 360 minutes
   B. 500 minutes
   C. 300 minutes
   D. 120 minutes

27. 450 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 45
   B. Ksh 4.50
   C. Ksh 0.45
   D. Ksh 5.50

28. You face the door and make a half turn. What do you face now? (1 mark)
   A. The door
   B. The ceiling
   C. The back wall
   D. The left wall only

29. A half turn makes (1 mark)
   A. a straight line
   B. a full turn
   C. a right angle
   D. a small angle

30. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. orange
   B. banana
   C. pawpaw
   D. mango

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Find the area of a square with 6 rows of 6 unit squares. Then find the area of a rectangle with 5 rows of 7 squares. Which is bigger? (4 marks)

32. Bags of 5 kg are filled from a 50 kg sack of rice. Find the number of bags. (2 marks)

33. How can you tell that a cuboid is a cube? Give one example of each from everyday life. (3 marks)

34. Work out 34 × 100 and 60 × 100. (2 marks)

35. Work out 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L. (3 marks)

36. Using each of the digits 4, 0, 7 and 2 once, write the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers you can make. (4 marks)

37. Ksh 3.50 is given as 3 shillings and 50 cents. Write 75 cents and 5 cents as decimals of a shilling. (3 marks)

38. Amina says the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm is 13 cm. Explain her mistake and give the correct perimeter. (3 marks)

39. State two things that are the same and two things that are different about a square and a rectangle. (4 marks)

40. Wanjiru buys goods worth Ksh 750 and pays with a Ksh 1,000 note. How much change should she get? Check your answer. (3 marks)

41. One layer of a cuboid has 15 blocks and the cuboid has 4 layers. Find the volume. Then find the volume if 2 more layers are added. (4 marks)

42. Wanjiru saves Ksh 250 every week. Write how much she has saved after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 weeks. State the rule. (3 marks)

43. A square garden has sides of 15 m. Find the perimeter of the garden. (2 marks)

44. Nanjala says an angle with longer arms is always bigger. Is she right? Explain. (3 marks)

45. Explain how a quarter turn is related to a right angle and how four quarter turns are related to a full turn. (3 marks)

46. A tank has 50 L of water. The family uses 18 L. How much water is left? (2 marks)

47. A garden bed has 9 rows and 4 columns of 1 m squares. Find its area in square metres. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It is even because it ends in 6
   Look at the ones digit. 6 is even, so 486 is even.

2. A — 742
   Compare the digits from the left. The largest number is 742.

3. B — Hundreds
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 8 is in the hundreds place.

4. B — one hundred and ninety
   190 = one hundred and ninety. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

5. D — 3,528
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 6,003 − 2,475 = 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.

6. C — 4,000
   The rule is subtract 250. 4,250 − 250 = 4,000.

7. D — 5/12
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 5/12 is less than one whole.

8. D — 2 1/3
   7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1. The whole number is 2 and the fraction is 1/3, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.

9. C — 9/9
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 9/9 is one whole or more.

10. A — 1/6
   The whole has 6 equal parts and 1 are shaded, so 1/6 is shaded.

11. D — 0.3
   Compare the tenths first. 0.3 is greater than 0.29.

12. D — 12 shillings and 50 cents
   The digits after the decimal point are the cents. Ksh 12.50 is 12 shillings and 50 cents.

13. B — 75/100
   The last digit of 0.75 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.75 = 75/100.

14. B — 0.07
   The digit 7 is in the hundredths place, so its total value is 0.07.

15. D — 13
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 13.

16. D — 24 cm
   A square has four equal sides. 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24.

17. A — 508 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 5 × 100 = 500, and 500 + 8 = 508. So the answer is 508 cm.

18. A — 20 m
   Add every side: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m.

19. D — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 8 − 1 = 7 cm.

20. D — A matchbox
   A matchbox has six rectangular faces, so it is a cuboid.

21. C — 8
   2 × 2 = 4 in a layer and 4 × 2 = 8 blocks.

22. A — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 4 kg − 1/4 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

23. C — 11:05
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 1 shows 1 × 5 = 5 minutes, so the time is 11:05.

24. B — 1 h 30 min
   90 ÷ 60 = 1 remainder 30, so 90 minutes = 1 h 30 min.

25. B — 2 h 40 min
   Count on from 9:30 a.m. to 12:10 p.m.. The total is 2 h 40 min.

26. C — 300 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 5 × 60 = 300 minutes.

27. B — Ksh 4.50
   450 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 50, so it is Ksh 4.50.

28. C — The back wall
   A half turn takes you to face the opposite way.

29. A — a straight line
   A half turn is two right angles, which form a straight line.

30. D — mango
   The biggest number is 4, which belongs to mango.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Square 36, rectangle 35. The square is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each area and 1 mark for the comparison and 1 mark for the difference.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: 10 bags
   Working / marking points: 50 ÷ 5 = 10. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: In a cube the length, width and height are equal. Example of a cube: a dice. Example of a cuboid that is not a cube: a matchbox or a brick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the property, 1 mark for each example.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3,400 and 6,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. Move each digit two places left.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); answer 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Largest: 7,420. Smallest: 2,047.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 7,420 (digits in descending order). 2 marks for 2,047 (a 4-digit number cannot begin with 0).

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.75 and 0.05 of a shilling (Ksh 0.75 and Ksh 0.05)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the idea that 100 cents = 1 shilling, 1 mark for each decimal.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added only two sides. The perimeter is the distance all the way round, so we add all four sides: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the reason, 1 mark for 26 cm.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Same: both have four straight sides and four right angles. Different: a square has all four sides equal and 4 lines of symmetry, but a rectangle has only opposite sides equal and 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for two similarities and 2 marks for two differences.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 250. Check: 750 + 250 = 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1,000 − 750, 1 mark for Ksh 250, 1 mark for the check.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: 60 blocks; then 90 blocks
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (2 marks); 6 layers: 15 × 6 = 90 (2 marks).

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 250, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,250. Rule: add 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for correct numbers.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60 m
   Working / marking points: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60 m. 1 mark for method and 1 mark for answer with unit.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: No. The size of an angle depends on how far apart the arms are, not on how long they are.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no, 1 mark for the opening between the arms, 1 mark for length not mattering.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quarter turn makes a right angle. Four quarter turns, that is four right angles, make a full turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for quarter turn = right angle, 1 mark for four quarters, 1 mark for full turn.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: 32 L
   Working / marking points: 50 − 18 = 32. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: 36 square metres
   Working / marking points: 9 × 4 = 36. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for the unit.
